candidates.rationale: Weakness: the IC decays across the sample (+0.0250 in 2000 down to +0.0027 and +0.0010 in 2012-13) with a 19.3-day half-life. The component responsible is the 21-day range window: a one-month stochastic is a short-horizon reversal proxy that was progressively arbitraged away in the later years. Re-cutting all three lookbacks to 126 days asks the same position question at a slower horizon that the fast crowd does not trade. Three literal edits, nothing else touched; changing all three is also the minimum that leaves no 4+ node block shared with the parent (the parent's numerator and guarded denominator are 5 and 9 nodes).

Weakness: |rho| 0.794 against the archived range/volume correlation, one tick from the 0.80 gate, plus 5/5 fields costing 0.200 of fitness. Both come from the same node, $dollar_volume / ($open + 1e-8): dividing by a single day's open just reconstructs share volume, leaving a price/size level in the series and making the leg a near-copy of the archive neighbour's TS_CORR($volume, $high - $low, 42). Normalising dollar volume by its own 63-day mean makes it a scale-free liquidity-surprise series per name and drops $open (5 -> 4 fields, charge 0.200 -> 0.100). Numerator field kept, denominator family changed, as the working memory requires for novelty.

Weakness: stability 0.86, negative in 2003 (-0.0051) and 2013 (-0.0013) - a regime problem, not a cost problem. The component responsible is the raw $volume level: volume levels and ranges rise and fall together with the volatility regime, so the correlation's cross-sectional meaning inverts when the regime turns. A 5-day change in dollar volume is a flow innovation with the level removed, so the correlation measures whether range expansion is being met by new flow rather than by standing size. One argument replaced; the archive's TS_DELTA($volume, 1) variant differs in both field and window, and the only shared block left is $high - $low at 3 nodes.

candidates.changed_node: the range numerator $high - $low -> $high - DELAY($low, 5) (denominator window 10 -> 42 is the minimum edit to clear the 5-node guarded-denominator share with the parent)
candidates.rationale: Weakness: |rho| 0.789 against the archive neighbour, which shares the same same-day $high - $low range block; that block is what pins the correlation, and it is also why 2003 goes negative (a same-day range carries no direction). Replacing it with $high - DELAY($low, 5) turns the numerator into a five-day upside extension - direction plus range - which is a different construct from every archived range leg. The denominator window 10 -> 42 is the single extra edit needed to break the parent's 5-node TS_MEAN($open, 10) + 1e-8 block, and it matches the price base to the leg's 57-day half-life. Fields 4/5, depth 6.

candidates.changed_node: the price multiplier TS_MAX($high, 21) -> TS_MEAN($high, 63) (plus $roa -> $roe to clear the 4-node fundamental-leg share)
candidates.rationale: Weakness: the leg that does the work is the 63-day leverage delta, but it is multiplied by TS_MAX($high, 21) / ($open + 1e-8) - a 21-day extreme divided by a single day's open. That is an extreme-value statistic on a spot denominator, so it jumps on one bad open, and its 21-day horizon is mismatched with the 63-day fundamental it scales; the leg's 38-day half-life says the composite is held far longer than 21 days. candidates.changed_node: the data field of the position leg: $open/$low/$high -> $volume in all three leaves
candidates.rationale: Weakness: the price-position leg is the redundant half - |rho| 0.755 against an archive twin that is this exact expression at 126 days, so the leg adds nothing the archive does not already hold, and it is also what drives the highest turnover in the pool (0.134 one-way) off a spot $open against a 21-day floor. Weakness: t 4.52 is the weakest in the pool and the price leg is nearly inert - a 21-day mean high over the 21-day max high of the same window is bounded in a narrow band just under 1, so after CS_RANK it contributes almost no dispersion and the factor is close to CS_RANK($roa) alone. The responsible node is the denominator's window, not the numerator: extending TS_MAX to 126 days turns the ratio into distance from the six-month high, which has real cross-sectional spread and matches the 44.7-day half-life. The combiner also goes from product to difference: multiplied, the volatility rank only rescales the momentum leg (it is non-negative), which is why 2013 flips negative when low-vol names lead; subtracted, each leg carries its own weight. candidates.rationale: Weakness: IC half-life 7.5 days, by far the shortest in the pool, despite two of the three legs being quarterly-frequency fundamentals. The cause is the CS_ZSCORE(...) * CS_RANK(...) product: an unbounded z-score of a sparse leverage delta multiplied by a non-negative daily rank means the day-to-day variation of the composite is the daily range, while the slow fundamental only sets a sign - so the composite decays at the range's speed, not the fundamental's. Making the leverage leg an additive bounded rank lets each leg carry its own weight, and the price base 42 -> 126 slows the remaining fast leg. Depth also drops 6 -> 5.

prompt:
You are proposing quantitative factor expressions for US large-cap equities.

Universe and data
- S&P 500 point-in-time constituents, roughly 500 names per day.
- Daily bars only, plus point-in-time quarterly fundamentals stamped from the
  report date. Every field is referenced with a leading `$`:
    $open $high $low $close $adj_close $volume $dollar_volume $return
    $roa $roe $operating_margin $leverage $asset_turnover
    $book_per_share $earnings_per_share $accrual_gap
  A bare name such as `close` is not a field and will be rejected.
- Execution convention: the signal is computed after the close of day T and the
  position is entered at the open of T+1.
- The window these factors are fitted and judged on runs from 2000 to 2013.
  Do not reason about anything later; you will never be shown a number from
  outside that window.

Syntax
- Operators are function calls: TS_MEAN, TS_STD, TS_MAX, TS_MIN, TS_RANK,
  TS_DELTA, TS_CORR, TS_COV, TS_SUM, TS_PRODUCT, TS_ARGMAX, TS_ARGMIN,
  TS_DECAY_LINEAR, EMA, DELAY, DELTA, RANK, ZSCORE, CS_RANK, CS_ZSCORE,
  CS_DEMEAN, IF, IF_ELSE, MIN, MAX, ABS, SIGN, LOG, LN, SQRT, POWER, BOUND,
  COUNT.
- Lookback windows must be positive integer literals, e.g. TS_MEAN($close, 21).
- Guard every division with a small epsilon: `/ (TS_STD($close, 21) + 1e-8)`.
- Well-formed example: -RANK(TS_CORR(RANK($close), RANK($volume), 5))

Hard limits every proposal must satisfy, or it is rejected before it is scored
- at most 200 characters
- at most 5 distinct `$fields`
- at most 4 free numeric constants (lookback windows and
  the 1e-8 epsilon guard do not count)
- expression tree depth at most 6
- must not share a complete sub-expression of 4 or more
  nodes with any published Alpha101 formula, or with any factor already in the
  archive. Restating a published alpha is the one thing that is always rejected.
- must cover at least 90% of the panel
- absolute rank correlation below 0.80 against every archive member

Output
- Return valid JSON only, matching the supplied JSON schema. No prose outside it.


TASK: MUTATE. For each parent below, identify its single weakest component and
change ONLY that component.

A mutation is localized: the returned expression must be within
3 tree edits of its parent. Rewriting the idea is not a mutation
and will be rejected. Say which node you changed in `changed_node`, and put the
parent's id in `parent_ids`.

Read the diagnostics: a factor whose IC is positive in most years and negative in two has a regime problem, one with high turnover is paying costs it does not earn back, and one whose IC half-life is short is being asked to predict too far ahead. Change the component responsible for the specific weakness you name.
